title: Deep learning synthetic CT from MRI improves detection of sacroiliac joint lesions
summary: In a prospective study of 30 adults with suspected inflammatory sacroiliitis, MRI and CT were done the same day. Synthetic CT images were generated from MRI with a commercial deep learning-based image synthesis method. With CT as reference and blinded readers, synthetic CT was more accurate than T1-weighted MRI for erosion (94% vs 86%, P = .003) and sclerosis (97% vs 81%); erosion specificity was 96% vs 89% (P = .01). The sample is small and the commercial method is not named.
ai_technology: Commercial deep learning image synthesis generating synthetic CT from MRI

evidence.tested: Prospective same-day MRI and CT in 30 participants, blinded readers, CT consensus as reference.
evidence.unknown: Only 30 participants; the specific commercial model is not named; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning converts MRI scans into synthetic CT-like images that show bone lesions better.
